body:
## Reproduction

1. Commit a file such as `experiments/repro.md` or `experiments/repro.mjs`.
2. Push that commit directly to the default branch.
3. Observe that lint/test (and other change-gated jobs) run even though `experiments/` is documented as excluded.

The release workflow's gated job conditions contain an unconditional `github.event_name == 'push'` branch. It short-circuits before the outputs from `scripts/detect-code-changes.mjs` are consulted. Independently, extension outputs such as `docs-changed` (and `mjs-changed` where present) are computed from the raw changed-file list, so excluded paths can still activate jobs on pull requests.

## Expected

Excluded-only changes remain excluded on both pull requests and pushes. The exclusion list has one authoritative definition, or a policy test prevents drift. Unused detector outputs should be removed.

## Workaround

Avoid excluded-directory files with extensions consumed by job gates, and use PR events where possible. This does not prevent the unconditional direct-push bypass.

## Suggested fix

Filter ignored paths before computing every job-gating output, remove unconditional push alternatives from change-gated jobs while preserving `workflow_dispatch`, and add event-matrix regression tests covering PRs and pushes with `experiments/`, `dev/log/`, and `docs/case-studies/` files.

Found while investigating link-assistant/formal-ai#846. The template revision and complete CI-file audit will be preserved in that issue's case study.
title: CI: excluded paths bypass change detection on direct pushes
